prompt.text: Use code 1 for a table, 2 for a bar graph, 3 for a pictogram, 4 for a line graph and 5 for a pie chart. A charity has category totals 13, 27, 46 and 91; readers need to compare the sizes at a glance, and the charity does not want partial icons. For the reason code, use 1 if a pictogram cannot show four categories, 2 if these totals would need part-icons, or 3 if pictograms can show only data in time order. Enter a two-digit number: the first digit is the code of the most suitable display and the second digit is the reason code.

content.text: Decide what readers must do with these four totals.

These totals are not convenient multiples of an icon. The charity also wants separate totals compared at a glance. Choose the display that compares sizes against a common scale, then think about what would go wrong with icons.
A bar graph compares the four totals against one scale at a glance. These totals are not convenient multiples of an icon, so a pictogram would need part-icons, and the reason code is 2.
